stories.summary: A TechCrunch Equity podcast episode questions whether the development of superintelligent AI should be treated as inevitable. It points to safety incidents, including an OpenAI Hugging Face breach, as evidence of the risks of deploying systems that may exceed human capabilities. Host Rebecca Bellan discusses the control problem with AI researcher and U.S. Executive Director Connor Leahy.

stories.title: AI could kill all humans in next decade, warn experts: but how seriously should we take them?
stories.summary: Experts and industry insiders have issued severe warnings about artificial superintelligence, increasing pressure for tighter controls, The Guardian reports. Their scenarios range from a Chernobyl-scale disaster to a greater than 10% chance that AI could kill all humans within a decade. The article examines how seriously such forecasts should be taken.

stories.title: US allies lack resources to keep pace on AI, top Pentagon official says
stories.summary: The Pentagon's top artificial-intelligence official says close U.S. allies lack the resources, experience and scale to match the American military's adoption of AI. Cameron Stanley described the technology's capabilities as revolutionary and said Washington is working with NATO and Five Eyes partners to help them avoid mistakes made by the United States.

stories.title: How one woman’s Tesla was remotely controlled – and used to harass her – by an abusive ex-partner
stories.summary: A Sydney woman's former partner remotely used her Tesla to harass her, The Guardian reports. Enrico Pucci could control the car's speed, temperature and locks, and the vehicle's alarm sounded three times during the night after years of domestic abuse. The woman said she was too frightened to go outside because she feared he might be damaging the car.

stories.title: UK datacentres will create just 25% of jobs predicted by tech sector, analysis finds
stories.summary: Planned UK datacentres are likely to create about 10,400 direct jobs, only a quarter of the more than 40,000 projected by industry group TechUK, according to analysis reported by The Guardian. Environmental thinktank Verdant produced the lower estimate and warned that the facilities would consume large amounts of energy.

links.headline: UK datacentres will create just 25% of jobs predicted by tech sector, analysis finds
links.excerpt: Facilities likely to employ 10,400 workers, compared with 40,000 in industry estimates, thinktank says Datacentres in the UK will create just a quarter of the jobs predicted by the tech sector, while consuming vast amounts of energy, according to new research. Environmental thinktank Verdant predicts that all the datacentres currently planned are likely to directly employ 10,400 workers – compared with the more than 40,000 cited in projections by the industry lobby group TechUK.</
